claims.text: Minor alloying additions that lower stacking-fault energy will increase deformation-twin formation in FCC multi-component alloys during loading.
Deformation twins act as barriers to dislocation motion.
The obstruction of dislocation motion by deformation twins enhances strain hardening.
Enhanced twinning and strain hardening may improve ductility.
The proposed CoCrFeMnNi baseline has a relatively high stacking-fault energy.
The proposed baseline has minimal pre-existing deformation twins.
Minor Pd additions can systematically lower the stacking-fault energy of the baseline alloy.
Minor Cu additions can systematically lower the stacking-fault energy of the baseline alloy.
Lower stacking-fault energy reduces the energy barrier for deformation-twin formation.
Twin-induced obstruction of dislocations alters failure mechanisms relative to a higher-stacking-fault-energy baseline.
The modified alloy is expected to develop a significantly higher deformation-twin density than the baseline.
The modified alloy is expected to exhibit higher strain-hardening rates than the baseline.
The modified alloy is expected to show a change in failure mode indicative of improved ductility.
The proposed mechanism should apply when secondary-phase formation and grain-boundary segregation are not significant.
The proposed mechanism should apply to FCC multi-component alloys at room and moderately elevated temperatures.
Minor compositional changes may affect deformation mechanisms other than twinning.
